note: The key in-period view of 1812, the house George H. Wheeler built in 1884 (the Real Estate and Building Journal's permit of June 7, 1884: '3-story dwelling, 30x80'). Taken square to the front from across Prairie Avenue: its verticals are vertical and its horizontals level. It shows a raised basement of rock-faced stone and a stone first storey with a large round-arched window in a two-storey projection on the south and an arched entrance porch reached by a straight stair with solid balustrades on the north; brick second and third storeys banded and dressed in stone; a paired window a storey in the projection and over the entrance; an iron balcony on the projection's top under a large round-arched window with a fanlight, and a smaller arched window to its north; and a tall shaped (Flemish) gable over the whole front, its outline swelling from a kneeler at each corner to a pointed head under a finial, with a grid window of nine lights. A camera is solved from it: data/reference_views/wheeler_house_1812_prairie/levy_front.json.
what_it_supplies: the front's storey heights, the raised basement and the stair's rise, read at the front's plane
the south projection's width and height and its windows
the entrance's place on the north and the openings' places and sizes
the shaped gable's outline, its grid window and finial
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the print is monochrome, so every stone, brick and paint colour stays reconstructed
the side and rear walls, and the roof behind the gable except its two front corners
depth: how far the projection stands out is the 1911 sheet's
